title: Rose motif — freestanding
subtitle: A single in-the-round rose that stands upright without a backing, 6 cm
excerpt: The freestanding rose works petals directly into a spiral chain without stacking or rolling — each petal round is worked into the chain spaces of the previous, building from tight inner petals outward to open outer petals in a single piece. It stands upright on its own, making it suitable for corsages, headbands, and cake toppers.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 8 (1893), freestanding flower crochet chapter (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crocheted flower construction.
heroPrompt: A freestanding crochet rose in blush pink DK cotton, standing upright without any backing, photographed at a 45-degree angle on natural linen in soft daylight. 6 cm across, petals spiral outward from the tight centre.

chartDefinition.title: Rose motif — freestanding
chartDefinition.caption: Worked in three spiral rounds into a base chain ring. Round 1: tight dc edging. Round 2: htr petal arches into the dc base. Round 3: tr petal arches into the same dc base between round-2 petals.

glossaryTerms.definition: One step taller than a double crochet, one step shorter than a treble. UK half treble equals US half double crochet. Used for the inner petal arches of this rose.

content.text: The freestanding rose works two rounds of petal arches into the same dc base ring, offset from each other so round 2 petals sit between round 1 petals. The
half-treble

inner petals are shorter and sit upright; the treble outer petals curve outward. The base ring pulls into a cup shape as the petals are worked, holding the flower upright without any stiffening unless the cotton fibre needs it.

For a stiffer flower suitable as a hair accessory, spray lightly with fabric starch and pin the petals open over a small ball while damp. For a softer corsage or applique, the natural tension of the cotton is enough to hold the shape.

attrs.title: Materials for one rose
attrs.body: About 10 g of DK-weight cotton in one or two colours. A 4 mm crochet hook. Tapestry needle. Scissors. Optional: fabric starch for stiffening.

content.text: Gauge
Each finished freestanding rose measures 6 cm across and 3 cm tall in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.
Stitches used
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc) — UK; US "single crochet".
half treble (htr) — UK; US "half double crochet".
treble (tr) — UK; US "double crochet".
Pattern
Base ring
Ch 24. Sl st to first ch to join into a ring. Ch 1 (does not count as stitch). Work 24dc around the ring. Sl st to first dc. (24 dc.)
Round 2 — inner petals

Working into the front loops of the dc ring only: *Ch 5. Sl st into next dc. Into the ch-5 arch work (1htr, 3htr, 1htr). Sl st into next dc. Sk 2dc.* Repeat from * to * seven more times. (8 inner petals.)
Round 3 — outer petals

Working into the back loops of the dc ring (the loops left unworked in round 2): *Ch 7. Sl st into next dc. Into the ch-7 arch work (1tr, 5tr, 1tr). Sl st into next dc. Sk 1dc.* Repeat from * to * seven more times. (8 outer petals, sitting between and behind the inner petals.) Fasten off, leaving a 20 cm tail.
Shaping

Thread the 20 cm tail through a tapestry needle. Take 3 to 4 stitches through the centre base to pull it into a slight cup, coaxing the inner petals upright and the outer petals outward. Fasten off inside the base.

definition.title: Rose motif — freestanding
definition.caption: 24dc ring. Inner petals (round 2) into front loops: ch-5 arches with htr fills. Outer petals (round 3) into back loops: ch-7 arches with tr fills.

content.text: Care
Handwash in cool water with mild soap. Lay flat on a towel. Reshape the petals into their standing position while damp. If the flower was stiffened, re-spray with fabric starch after washing.
What to try next

A third petal round of double trebles (dtr) gives a fully open five-layer rose about 9 cm across. The same technique applied to a longer 36-chain ring produces a dahlia-style flower with more petals. See crochet-flower-dahlia for the dahlia variant.
